Account snapshot / CRM notes:
- Product: building a GitHub-style PR review assistant embedded in IDE + GitHub web UI. Focus = diff summarization, comment generation, prioritization (reranking) for noisy PRs.
- Key asks: low-latency streaming to IDE (sub-150ms token latency for completion), deterministic suggestions (model/version pinning), prefix & KV cache reuse across reviewers, multi-pass reranker to surface top 3 comments per file.
- Workload: mixed — real-time single-editor completions (low latency), and batch rerank jobs for nightly repo scans (throughput).
- Model preferences: want an open-model fallback but need Redwood-verified performance for mainline; CTO: "Deterministic suggestions — model pinning is a must. No silent model swaps."
- Security: SSO/SAML, enterprise KMS for key material, audit logging at token/request level, 1yr retention controls; plan to host evaluation inside VPC. Data residency: prefer NA only.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to commit to Dedicated if latency and pinning guarantees met. Concerned about per-token billshock on batch reranks.
- Integration: GitHub Apps + IDE plugin (VS Code/JetBrains), webhooks for PR events, ability to run inference on commit hooks or scheduled workers. SE asked about backpressure & graceful degradation policies (fallback models/regions).
- Evaluation criteria: 1) streaming latency (IDE), 2) end-to-end accuracy on 300-sample PR eval set (precision of suggested comments), 3) reranker recall/precision, 4) operational controls (pinning, rollbacks), 5) security posture (SOC2, KMS, VPC).
- Quote from CTO (Priya Rao): "We need stable, repeatable outputs for release notes and review suggestions — no surprises in QA. If Redwood can guarantee pinning + predictable latency we'll move to dedicated capacity."
- Planned POC: 2-week pilot across 3 engineering teams. Benchmarks include 95th p99 token latency, token-cost per review, and false-positive rate for comment generation.
